title: Work Tree sorting controls
description:
Add global sorting controls to the Work Tree so users can order features, phases, and tasks by criteria other than priority. The current `buildWorkTree` hardcodes `priority ASC → number ASC → createdAt → title`. The user reports seeing older tasks before newer ones because priority numbers can drift from creation order after drag-and-drop reorder or midpoint insert.

Scope:
- Add a sort selector in the dashboard Work Tree header/toolbar.
- Support per-level sort keys: priority, number (global sequence), createdAt, updatedAt, title, shortId.
- For tasks also support: startedAt, completedAt, status (workflow order).
- Provide asc/desc toggle.
- Persist the selected sort in `localStorage` per project (via `dashboard-storage.ts`).
- Keep the existing default behavior (`priority` asc) so current users see no change until they interact.
- Maintain responsive layout; the control must fit in the existing toolbar.

Non-scope:
- Server-side sorting (keep client-side only).
- Reordering the internal canonical priority field; this only changes presentation order.

Files likely to change:
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/dashboard-tree.ts` — accept sort options, build sorted tree accordingly.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/hooks/use-dashboard-tree.ts` — hold sort state, persist to localStorage.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx` — render sort controls.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/dashboard-storage.ts` — add storage key helpers if needed.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/types.ts` — possibly add a shared `SortKey`/`SortDirection` type.

Reference:
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/dashboard-tree.ts:buildWorkTree`
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/hooks/use-dashboard-tree.ts`
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx`

Behaviors to preserve: existing expand/collapse, filters, search, drag-and-drop, and mobile layout.

tasks.title: Polish Work Tree sort control styling
tasks.description:
Polish the styling of the Work Tree sort control so it does not look like the large filter chips below. From the screenshot, the current SortControl uses a full-width h-11 pill select and an equally wide direction pill, which looks clunky.

Target design:
- Compact single-line control that fits on mobile without wrapping.
- Smaller select (h-9 or h-10, rounded-lg, minimal padding, subtle border).
- Direction toggle as a small square/circle icon button (not a wide pill), with an SVG arrow (ChevronUp/ChevronDown or ArrowUp/ArrowDown from lucide-react) instead of the ↑/↓ unicode character.
- Keep label visible on desktop, hidden on mobile.
- Keep the control aligned with the search bar, above the filter chips.
- Preserve all existing behavior: options, direction toggle, localStorage persistence.

File:
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx (SortControl component and its container).

---
**Completion summary:**
Polished the Work Tree sort control styling.

Changes:
- Replaced large h-11 pill select/direction button with a compact inline control:
  - Small rounded container (h-9) matching the card surface.
  - Native select with custom ChevronDown icon, no field-control padding.
  - Tiny square direction toggle (h-6 w-6) with lucide-react sort icons.
  - Label inline on desktop, hidden on mobile.
- Changed the toolbar row to always flex-wrap instead of stacking on mobile.
- Removed unused Select component import from work-tree.tsx.
- Rebuilt and copied web-ui dist.

tasks.title: Fix Work Tree accordion expand/collapse for recently linked features
tasks.description:
Investigate and fix a bug in the dashboard Work Tree accordion where:
1. Clicking the down-arrow icon of an expanded feature no longer collapses the feature.
2. Features F011, F012, F013, F014 (recently linked to their parent features in the planner) do not expand at all in the Work Tree.

Code references to inspect:
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree-rows.tsx
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/hooks/use-dashboard-tree.ts
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/ui/accordion.tsx

Likely causes:
- State key mismatch after feature linking/renumbering.
- Accordion toggle handler bound to wrong element or event propagation stopped.
- Feature rows filtered out or rendered without children due to stale tree data.
- Feature done-status auto-collapse logic interfering with user toggle.

Acceptance: all features expand/collapse on arrow click; recently linked features (F011-F014) render their phases and tasks; no horizontal overflow or layout regression.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed Work Tree accordion toggle in packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree-rows.tsx. Feature and phase chevron buttons now stop event propagation on click and pointerDown, preventing dnd-kit sortable wrapper from intercepting toggles. This restores expand/collapse for all features, including done features F011-F014 collapsed by default. Build passes with pnpm --filter @agent-plan/web-ui build. Headless smoke test not run due to missing browser harness; user should verify in browser after rebuilding web-ui.
tasks.notes:
Investigated Work Tree accordion toggle issue.

Suspected cause: feature/phase rows are wrapped in dnd-kit SortableItem. The PointerSensor or the sortable wrapper can intercept/interfere with click events on the chevron toggle button, especially on repeated interactions, making the button feel unresponsive.

Fix applied in packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree-rows.tsx:
- Added e.stopPropagation() in onClick for both FeatureTreeRow and PhaseTreeRow chevron buttons.
- Added onPointerDown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()} to prevent dnd-kit from capturing the pointer event on the toggle.

This should restore collapse/expand on arrow click, including for done features (F011-F014) which are collapsed by default in "all" open mode.

Build passes (pnpm --filter @agent-plan/web-ui build). Manual verification in browser still needed because no headless browser/test harness is available in the workspace.

tasks.title: Fix header active-task locate icon click does nothing
tasks.description:
User reports that clicking the target/locate icon on an in-progress task in the top header active-tasks bar does nothing. Expected behavior: navigate to the dashboard and scroll to/highlight the task in the Work Tree (via ?locate=T00x query param or equivalent).

Code references to inspect:
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx (active tasks header bar)
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx (locate param handler)
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/hooks/use-dashboard-tree.ts
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/api.ts

Likely causes:
- onClick handler missing or broken
- navigate() not called with correct location
- locate effect in WorkTree not triggering because the route is not dashboard
- event propagation blocked

Acceptance: clicking the target icon for an active task navigates to dashboard Work Tree, expands the task's feature+phase, scrolls to the task row, and pulses/highlight it.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed locate-in-work-tree scroll.

Root causes:
1. TaskTreeRow never rendered `id={`task-row-${task.number}`}`, so WorkTree's locate effect could never find the target DOM element.
2. Locate effect set treeOpenMode("all"), which auto-collapses done features and races with the explicit feature expansion.

Changes:
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree-rows.tsx: pass `id={`task-row-${task.number}`}` to StatusItem.
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/ui/status-item.tsx: forward optional `id` prop to the root div.
- packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx: use treeOpenMode("smart") in locate effect to preserve explicit expansions.

Build passes (pnpm --filter @agent-plan/web-ui build). Browser verification recommended.

---
**Completion summary:**
Locate icon now works after copying the updated Vite bundle to packages/pi-adapter/web-ui-dist via scripts/copy-web-ui.sh and reloading the browser. Root fix was restoring the missing id={`task-row-${task.number}`} on TaskTreeRow (lost during StatusItem refactor) and forwarding id through StatusItem.
